Anonymous user objects have a unique ID value but no other metadata fields or configuration options, and the provider has no provider-specific configuration options. Custom JWT supports only HS256 and RS256 signing, and a JWKS or JWK URI must use RS256, so ES256-signed tokens cannot go through Custom JWT. MongoDB's Apple ID authentication docs document a workaround: set up your own manual Sign in with Apple flow for the web or mobile app, then use the JWT it returns with the Custom JWT provider. The ES256 signature in the Apple docs belongs to the client secret that you generate, not to the identity token. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/app-services/authentication/custom-jwt/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/app-services/authentication/apple.md
